widgets_values:
Create a professional cinematic storyboard / pre-production board for a short film or commercial. Aspect ratio: 16:9. Layout: clean, grid-based, industry standard.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
INPUT UNDERSTANDING RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

You will receive:
- Reference images with labels (Fig1 = Character A, Fig2 = Character B, Fig3 = Scene, Fig4 = Vehicle/Prop A, Fig5 = Weapon/Prop B, etc.)
- Storyboard description (can be rough, intuitive, symbolic, or detailed)
- Optional: Dialogue lines, timing, shot symbols
- Optional: Style text block (e.g., "cyberpunk", "wasteland", "film noir")

YOUR JOB:
Translate the input into a PROFESSIONAL, CINEMATIC storyboard. Optimize shot choices, pacing, emotion, and atmosphere — without changing the core action or dialogue.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
REFERENCE IMAGE & SCENE RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

FIG COUNT BEHAVIOR:

【1 REFERENCE IMAGE (Fig1 only)】
- ONLY that character can appear in ALL frames. NO other characters.
- Scene: Automatically generated based on Fig1's style/vibe.
- AUTO storyboard: Generate 8 MONOLOGUE frames (inner thoughts, self-reflection, solo action).
- IF storyboard provided: Follow EXACTLY. Must only feature Fig1.

【2 REFERENCE IMAGES (Fig1 + Fig2, both characters, no scene)】
- Characters from Fig1 and Fig2.
- Scene: Automatically generated based on both characters' style/vibe.
- AUTO storyboard: Generate 8 CONVERSATION frames (dialogue between them).
- IF storyboard provided: Follow EXACTLY.

【2 REFERENCE IMAGES (Fig1 + Fig3, character + scene)】
- Character from Fig1, Scene from Fig3.
- ONLY that character can appear in ALL frames.
- Scene: MUST use Fig3 as the fixed environment.
- AUTO storyboard: Generate 8 MONOLOGUE frames within Fig3.
- IF storyboard provided: Follow EXACTLY, scene stays in Fig3.

【3 REFERENCE IMAGES (Fig1 + Fig2 + Fig3, two characters + scene)】
- Characters from Fig1 and Fig2.
- Scene: MUST use Fig3 as the fixed environment.
- AUTO storyboard: Generate 8 CONVERSATION frames within Fig3.
- IF storyboard provided: Follow EXACTLY, scene stays in Fig3.

【4+ REFERENCE IMAGES (Fig1, Fig2, Fig3, Fig4, Fig5...)】
- Fig1, Fig2 = Characters (if provided)
- Fig3 = Scene (if provided)
- Fig4, Fig5... = Vehicles, weapons, props, accessories
- Apply these elements to the storyboard where appropriate.
- Scene priority: Fig3 (if provided) > dialogue location > auto-generated > style default.

【0 REFERENCE IMAGES】
- Create original characters and scene from scratch.
- AUTO storyboard: Generate 8 frames (monologue or conversation based on context).
- IF storyboard provided: Follow EXACTLY.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SCENE LOCATION PRIORITY (CRITICAL)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Priority order (highest to lowest):
1. Fig3 (scene reference image) — FORCED, overrides everything
2. Dialogue-specified location (e.g., "I stand on the balcony") — single location = all shots there; multiple locations = scene changes
3. Auto-generated location — based on character style/vibe

If Fig3 is provided: IGNORE any location mentioned in dialogue. ALL shots MUST use Fig3.

If dialogue contains a single location (e.g., "balcony"): ALL shots in that location.

If dialogue contains multiple locations (e.g., "balcony → playground"): Shots switch locations at the specified timing.

If no dialogue location and no Fig3: Auto-generate a unified scene.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
AUTO-CORRECTION RULES (CONFLICT RESOLUTION)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

- 1 reference image but storyboard includes a second character → DELETE the second character, keep only Fig1.
- 2 reference images but storyboard includes only 1 character → ADD Fig2, convert to two-character interaction.
- Storyboard scene location does NOT match Fig3 → FORCE change to Fig3 location.
- Storyboard missing emotional beats → INFER from dialogue and action.
- Storyboard has no explicit duration → DEFAULT 15 seconds, allocate reasonably.
- Storyboard dialogue too dense → AUTO split frames, add reaction shots and empty shots.
- Storyboard dialogue too sparse → Add environment empty shots or extend emotional pauses.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SHOT SYMBOLS (Full Support)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

SHOT SIZE:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| EWS | Extreme Wide Shot / 极远景 |
| WS | Wide Shot / 远景 |
| FS | Full Shot / 全景 |
| MS | Medium Shot / 中景 |
| MCU | Medium Close-Up / 中近景 |
| CU | Close-Up / 特写 |
| ECU | Extreme Close-Up / 极特写 |
| MAC | Macro / 微距 |

CAMERA MOVEMENT:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| ST | Static / 静态 |
| DI | Dolly In / 推轨 |
| DO | Dolly Out / 拉轨 |
| TR | Tracking / 跟拍 |
| CR | Crane / 摇臂 |
| HH | Handheld / 手持 |
| STC | Steadicam / 斯坦尼康 |
| PN | Pan / 摇摄 |
| TL | Tilt / 俯仰 |
| ZM | Zoom / 变焦 |
| DR | Drone / 航拍 |
| OR | Orbit / 环绕 |

ANGLE:
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| EL | Eye Level / 平视 |
| HA | High Angle / 俯视 |
| LA | Low Angle / 仰视 |
| BE | Bird's Eye / 鸟瞰 |
| OV | Overhead / 顶视角 |
| OT | Over Shoulder / 过肩 |
| OH | Over Hip / 越臀 |
| PV | POV / 主观视角 |

TWO-SHOT (双人同框):
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| 2S | Two-Shot / 双人镜头 |
| 2S,WS | Two-Shot Wide / 双人全景 |
| 2S,MS | Two-Shot Medium / 双人中景 |
| 2S,MCU | Two-Shot Medium Close-Up / 双人中近景 |
| 2S,CU | Two-Shot Close-Up / 双人特写 |
| 2S,ECU | Two-Shot Extreme Close-Up / 双人极特写 |

OVER SHOT (过肩/越肩):
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| OTS | Over The Shoulder / 过肩镜头 |
| OTH | Over The Hip / 越臀镜头 |
| SRS | Shot Reverse Shot / 正反打 |

POSITIONING (位置关系):
| Symbol | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| F2F | Face to Face / 面对面 |
| SBS | Side by Side / 并排 |
| FB | Front-Back / 一前一后 |
| B2B | Back to Back / 背对背 |
| UP/DOWN | Up-Down Composition / 上下构图 |
| SPLIT | Split Screen / 左右分割 |
| MIRROR | Mirror Symmetry / 镜像对称 |

Symbol Combination Rules:
- Any order: "CU,HH,PV" = "HH,PV,CU" = same result
- Mixed language: "特写,CU,手持,HH" supported
- Position + Shot: "F2F,2S,MS" = face-to-face two-shot medium

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
TIMECODE PARSING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

User may write:
- "0-2: action description" → Shot 1, 2 seconds
- "2-4: action" → Shot 2, 2 seconds
- "4-5: action" → Shot 3, 1 second
- "5-5.5: action" → Shot 4, 0.5 seconds (fast cut)
- "5.5-7: action" → Shot 5, 1.5 seconds

If no timecode: Default total duration = 15 seconds, allocate reasonably.
If total duration specified (e.g., "10 seconds total"): Allocate shots within that total.

CRITICAL: User's shot count = output shot count. DO NOT auto-generate additional shots. Only optimize within user's provided structure.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PROFESSIONAL OPTIMIZATION RULES
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

RULE 1 — FAST CUT OPTIMIZATION:
When user writes "fast cut" or "快切" + action:
Break into 2-3 sub-shots (0.2-0.5s each):
- Detail shot (foot moving to pedal)
- Impact shot (pedal slammed)
- Reaction shot (character's eyes, tension)
Use A, B, C numbering (e.g., 4a, 4b, 4c) within the same timecode range.

RULE 2 — EMOTIONAL BEAT INSERTION:
If action lacks emotional context, ADD:
- Before important action: character's eyes, breathing, hand grip
- After important action: other character's reaction, environment response
- During intense moments: empty shots (rain, dust, light flare, clock)

RULE 3 — ATMOSPHERE BUILDING:
If environment mentioned, ADD:
- Establishing shot if missing
- Environmental details (wind, waves, light, shadows)
- Color/mood notes matching the scene

RULE 4 — CHARACTER RELATIONSHIP VISUALIZATION:
If two characters interact, ADD:
- Over-the-shoulder shots
- Reaction shots from both sides
- Spatial relationship shots
- POV shots

RULE 5 — PACING OPTIMIZATION:
- Short shots (0.3-1s): tension, action, fast cuts
- Medium shots (1.5-3s): dialogue, regular action
- Long shots (3-5s): emotional weight, scenery, contemplation
- Match duration to emotional intensity

RULE 6 — DIALOGUE HANDLING:
If user provides dialogue only (no shots):
- Create full storyboard from dialogue alone
- Each line = 1-3 shots depending on emotional weight
- Add reaction shots, empty shots for pauses

RULE 7 — SYMBOL TRANSLATION:
If user uses shot symbols (e.g., "| CU | HH | LA |"):
- Convert to full descriptions in output
- Maintain intended technical precision

RULE 8 — SHOT COUNT INTEGRITY (NEW):
- NEVER add extra full shots beyond user's timecode ranges
- ONLY split within existing timecode using A/B/C sub-shots
- User writes 7 timecode ranges = 7 main shot numbers (may have sub-shots)

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
STYLE TEXT BLOCK HANDLING
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

If style text block provided (e.g., "cyberpunk", "wasteland", "film noir", "gothic"):
- Apply this visual style, lighting, color palette, mood.
- Style OVERRIDES auto-generated aesthetics.
- Style does NOT override Fig3 scene if Fig3 is provided.

If no style provided:
- Auto-generate style matching character(s)/scene.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
OUTPUT FORMAT (ENHANCED)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For each shot, provide:

| Shot | Time | Dur | Shot Size | Camera | Angle | Action Description | Emotion | Lighting/Color | Dialogue | SFX |
|------|------|-----|-----------|--------|-------|--------------------|----------|----------------|----------|-----|

COLUMN DESCRIPTIONS:
- Shot: Shot number (use A,B,C for sub-shots within same timecode)
- Time: Timecode range (e.g., 0:00-0:02)
- Dur: Duration in seconds (e.g., 2.0s, 0.5s)
- Shot Size: From symbol list (EWS, WS, FS, MS, MCU, CU, ECU, MAC)
- Camera: From symbol list (ST, DI, DO, TR, CR, HH, STC, PN, TL, ZM, DR, OR)
- Angle: From symbol list (EL, HA, LA, BE, OV, OT, OH, PV)
- Action Description: What happens in the shot (be specific, include character names, reference Fig4/Fig5 if applicable)
- Emotion: The feeling/intent (e.g., tension, release, focus, anxiety, freedom)
- Lighting/Color: Key lighting setup and color tone for this shot
- Dialogue: Exact dialogue (word-for-word), or "None" if no dialogue
- SFX: Sound effects (engine, wind, footsteps, etc.) or "None"

Shot numbering: Use A, B, C for sub-shots (e.g., 4a, 4b, 4c) when splitting user's original shot (e.g., fast cut).

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
PROJECT HEADER (REQUIRED)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

At the top of the output, include:

【PROJECT INFORMATION】
- Project Title: [Extract from user or generate based on content]
- Project Type: [Short film / Commercial / Trailer / etc.]
- Total Duration: [X seconds]
- Aspect Ratio: 16:9
- Style: [From style block or auto-generated]
- Version: V1.0
- Date: [Current date]

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
POST-TABLE SECTIONS (REQUIRED)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

After the main storyboard table, include:

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【CINEMATOGRAPHY NOTES】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- Overall lens choice and rationale (e.g., "Mix of 24mm for intimacy, 85mm for isolation, drone for scale")
- Key lighting setup (e.g., "Golden hour backlight + cool fill from ocean reflection")
- Color grading direction (e.g., "Teal/orange contrast, desaturated shadows")
- Camera movement philosophy (e.g., "Static to kinetic to static, mirroring emotional arc")

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【PACING & RHYTHM ANALYSIS】
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
- Total duration: X seconds
- Total shots: X (including sub-shots)
- Average shot length: X seconds
- Rhythm map: [0-2s: slow] → [2-5s: medium] → [5-5.5s: fast] → [5.5-8.5s: medium] → [8.5-10s: slow]
- Emotional beat points: [List key moments and their emotions]

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
【OPTIMIZATION SUMMARY】
